data.name: Grishika
data.gender_notes: Grishika is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Grishika is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Grishas’ meaning ‘grids’ or ‘geometrical designs’. In Hindu mythology, it is believed that the goddess Grishika embodies the protective power of these geometric designs. She is often depicted as a goddess of protection, particularly for children. The name Grishika carries the meaning “Goddess of Grids, Protection” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Grishika usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of grids, protection and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of protection and order in the universe

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Grishika total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Grishika underscores the rich Hindu tradition of geometrical patterns and symbols. It highlights the belief in the sufficiency and power of these designs as a representation of the divine. Moreover, it highlights the significance of the goddess Grishika, who represents the protective force of these designs. This name adds to the cultural diversity and complexity of the Hindu faith, celebrating its deep connection to symbolism and the divine.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Grishika holds profound spiritual significance in Hinduism as it is believed to be a manifestation of the protective goddess, who bestows safety and security. This name instills a sense of peace and reassurance, evoking the understanding that even in the face of challenges and uncertainties, there is a higher power that shields and cares for us..
data.spiritual_symbolism: Grishika represents the feminine aspect of life, embodied in the sacred river Ganga. Her name signifies purity, grace, and the transformative power of water, washing away impurities and bestowing blessings.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Grishika was one of the 16 Maharajadhikas (great rulers) of Jodhpur during the medieval period. The name Grishika carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Grishika was a significant ruler in the Rajput kingdom of Jodhpur. Her exact reign is not known but she is believed to have ruled in the 15th or 16th century.

historical_references.reference: Grishika is mentioned in the epic Mahabharata as the wife of Bhishma Pitamaha and the mother of Vidura.
historical_references.context: Grishika was an important character in Hindu mythology. She is mentioned in the Mahabharata as the wife of Bhishma Pitamaha and the mother of Vidura, one of the key characters in the epic.

modern_usage.modern_context: Grishika is a name in Hindu mythology and religion, often referred to as the goddess of snakes and rain. She is worshipped during the monsoon season and is associated with fertility and creation. Her modern context can be seen on various platforms including Indian mythology and religion, Indian folklore and literature, and art and culture.
